Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from the Acme security side: 

1) Regional requirements
- We need guaranteed storage of customer-derived PII within the legal region of the customer (EU customers' data must remain in EU regions; US customers' data in US regions).

2) Failover & DR
- Cross-region failover is allowed only under explicit DR scenarios and must be configurable per-tenant. During failover, we require that replicated backups remain within the same legal region where possible.
- Can Redwood guarantee that failover will not route EU-customer requests to a US-hosted pool by default? If not, what controls are exposed to us?

3) Backups & snapshots
- Backups must be stored in region or in customer-controlled S3 with SSE-KMS. Are snapshots encrypted and region-scoped?

4) Audit/logging
- We need the option to disable or redact request-level logs for sensitive traffic and an ability to set retention (30/90/365 days). Provide capabilities and any caveats (e.g., when logs are required for support).

Hi John — thanks for the detailed questions. Answers below (TL;DR: yes on per-tenant region pinning; failover and backups are configurable, with some operational caveats):

1) Region pinning
- Redwood supports per-tenant routing policies. You can pin a tenant to one or more regions. All inference requests for that tenant are routed to the pinned region(s) unless a policy allows failover.
- For models that use persistent KV caches, those caches are stored in the same region as the tenant and are not replicated cross-region unless you opt into geo-replication.

2) Failover behavior
- Failover is opt-in per-tenant. Two modes:
  a) manual failover (preferred for strict compliance): operations trigger failover to a listed secondary region;
  b) automated failover: health-based fallback to secondary regional pool — only if you enable it.
- By default, Acme's pinned EU tenants will not route to US pools unless you explicitly enable an EU->US failover policy.

3) Backups & snapshots
- Snapshots of model artifacts and tenant data can be configured to land in a customer-controlled S3 bucket in the chosen region. We support SSE-KMS (customer-managed keys) for these buckets.
- Redwood-managed backups are stored encrypted and region-scoped; we can provide encryption-at-rest and ensure replica placement remains within the legal region, subject to available infrastructure.

4) Audit/logging & retention
- Request-level logs can be configured at the tenant or API key level. Options: keep full logs, redact PII fields, or disable body-level logs (keep only metadata).
- Retention windows configurable (30/90/365d). Note: when logs are disabled/redacted, some troubleshooting data may be unavailable for support; we document trade-offs in the FAQ.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-FAQ.docx (contains config snippets and sample policies).
